The **Women's Team Archery event** at the **2012 Summer Olympics** in **London** was one of the most exciting competitions in the sport, featuring top archers from around the world. Here’s a detailed breakdown of everything you need to know:

---

### **1. Event Overview**
- **Discipline:** Recurve (Olympic-style archery)
- **Format:** Team event (3 archers per country)
- **Dates:** **July 27–29, 2012** (Qualification on July 27, Elimination rounds on July 29)
- **Venue:** **Lord’s Cricket Ground** (a historic venue, making it a unique setting for archery)
- **Number of Teams:** **12 teams** (36 archers total)

---

### **2. Qualification & Participating Teams**
Teams qualified based on performances at the **2011 World Archery Championships** and continental qualification tournaments. The **12 teams** that competed were:

| **Country**       | **Archers**                          | **Notes** |
|-------------------|--------------------------------------|-----------|
| **South Korea**   | Ki Bo-bae, Choi Hyeonju, Lee Sung-jin | Defending champions (2008 Beijing) |
| **China**         | Cheng Ming, Fang Yuting, Xu Jing     | Silver medalists in 2008 |
| **Japan**         | Ren Hayakawa, Miki Kanie, Kaori Kawanaka | Strong dark horse |
| **Russia**        | Ksenia Perova, Kristina Timofeeva, Inna Stepanova | Bronze in 2008 |
| **Denmark**       | Carina Christiansen, Maja Jager, Louise Laursen | First Olympic team appearance |
| **India**         | Deepika Kumari, Bombayla Devi Laishram, Chekrovolu Swuro | Historic first team medal (bronze) |
| **Italy**         | Pia Lionetti, Jessica Tomasi, Natalia Valeeva | Veteran presence |
| **Great Britain** | Naomi Folkard, Amy Oliver, Alison Williamson | Host nation |
| **Chinese Taipei**| Tan Ya-ting, Le Chien-ying, Lin Chia-en | Strong individual performers |
| **Mexico**        | Mariana Avitia, Aída Román, Alejandra Valencia | Rising archery nation |
| **Ukraine**       | Tetyana Dorokhova, Kateryna Palekha, Lidiia Sichenikova | Consistent performers |
| **USA**           | Miranda Leek, Khatuna Lorig, Jennifer Nichols | Veteran Khatuna Lorig (5-time Olympian) |

---

### **3. Competition Format**
#### **Qualification Round (July 27, 2012)**
- Each archer shot **72 arrows** (12 ends of 6 arrows) at a distance of **70 meters**.
- The **top 4 teams** received a **bye** into the quarterfinals.
- The remaining **8 teams** competed in a **1/8 elimination round** (best-of-24 arrows).

#### **Elimination Rounds (July 29, 2012)**
- **1/8 Elimination (if needed):** Best of 24 arrows (8 arrows per archer).
- **Quarterfinals, Semifinals, Bronze & Gold Medal Matches:**
  - Best of **24 arrows** (8 per archer, alternating shots).
  - If tied, a **sudden-death shoot-off** (1 arrow per archer, closest to center wins).

---

### **4. Results & Key Moments**
#### **Quarterfinals**
- **South Korea** def. **Denmark** (208–194)
- **China** def. **Italy** (200–199) – *Narrow win*
- **Japan** def. **Ukraine** (207–192)
- **Russia** def. **Great Britain** (215–208) – *Hosts eliminated*

#### **Semifinals**
- **South Korea** def. **Japan** (221–206) – *Dominant performance*
- **China** def. **Russia** (208–207) – *Dramatic 1-point win*

#### **Bronze Medal Match**
- **Japan** vs. **Russia**
  - **Japan won 209–207** in a close match, securing their first Olympic team medal in archery.

#### **Gold Medal Match**
- **South Korea** vs. **China**
  - **South Korea won 210–209** in a **thrilling shoot-off**.
    - Both teams tied at **209** after 24 arrows.
    - **Shoot-off:** Each archer shot **1 arrow**.
      - **Ki Bo-bae (KOR)** hit the **10-ring (X-center)**, while **Cheng Ming (CHN)** hit a **9**.
      - **South Korea won gold by 1 point** (29–28 in the shoot-off).

---

### **5. Medalists**
| **Medal** | **Team**       | **Archers**                          |
|-----------|----------------|--------------------------------------|
| **Gold**  | **South Korea** | Ki Bo-bae, Choi Hyeonju, Lee Sung-jin |
| **Silver**| **China**      | Cheng Ming, Fang Yuting, Xu Jing     |
| **Bronze**| **Japan**      | Ren Hayakawa, Miki Kanie, Kaori Kawanaka |

---

### **6. Notable Facts & Highlights**
- **South Korea’s Dominance:**
  - Won their **7th consecutive Olympic team gold** (since 1988).
  - Ki Bo-bae later won **individual gold** in London.
- **India’s Historic Bronze:**
  - India’s **first-ever Olympic medal in archery** (team or individual).
  - Deepika Kumari was a rising star (though she underperformed in the individual event).
- **Close Matches:**
  - The **gold medal match** was decided by a **single point** in the shoot-off.
  - China nearly upset South Korea but fell just short.
- **Host Nation Disappointment:**
  - Great Britain was eliminated in the quarterfinals.
- **Khatuna Lorig’s Legacy:**
  - The **USA’s Khatuna Lorig** (a 5-time Olympian) competed in her **4th Olympics** (previously for the Unified Team in 1992).
- **Lord’s Cricket Ground:**
  - The iconic venue hosted archery for the first time, with temporary stands set up on the outfield.

---

### **7. Records & Statistics**
- **Highest Team Score in Qualification:**
  - **South Korea (2,018/2,160)** – *Olympic record at the time*.
- **Lowest Qualifying Team to Medal:**
  - **Japan (1,965)** – Finished 5th in qualification but won bronze.
- **Most Arrows in 10-Ring (Qualification):**
  - **Ki Bo-bae (KOR)** – 40/72 (55.6%).
- **Shoot-Off Drama:**
  - The **gold medal match** was the **first team final in Olympic history** to go to a shoot-off.

---

### **8. Aftermath & Legacy**
- **South Korea’s Continued Success:**
  - They would go on to win **team gold again in 2016 (Rio)** and **2020 (Tokyo)**.
- **Ki Bo-bae’s Career:**
  - Became one of the greatest archers of all time, winning **4 Olympic golds** (2012 team & individual, 2016 team & mixed team).
- **India’s Archery Growth:**
  - The bronze medal **inspired a new generation** of Indian archers, including **Deepika Kumari**, who later became a world champion.
- **Japan’s Rise:**
  - Japan’s bronze was a sign of their growing strength, leading to **team silver in 2020 (Tokyo)**.

---

### **9. Where Are They Now? (2024 Update)**
| **Archer**          | **Country** | **Post-2012 Career** |
|---------------------|------------|----------------------|
| **Ki Bo-bae**       | South Korea | Retired in 2021, now a coach. |
| **Choi Hyeonju**    | South Korea | Competed in 2016, now a commentator. |
| **Lee Sung-jin**    | South Korea | Retired, works in sports administration. |
| **Cheng Ming**      | China      | Competed in 2016, now a coach. |
| **Deepika Kumari**  | India      | Competed in 2016 & 2020, still active. |
| **Ren Hayakawa**    | Japan      | Competed in 2016 & 2020, retired in 2021. |
| **Khatuna Lorig**   | USA        | Competed in 2016, retired, now a coach. |

---

### **10. Fun Facts**
- **First Olympic Archery at Lord’s:**
  - The venue is more famous for cricket, but archery was a **huge success**, with sell-out crowds.
- **South Korea’s "Archery Dynasty":**
  - Since 1988, South Korea has **only lost one Olympic team gold** (1992, when they didn’t compete as a unified team).
- **India’s Medal Drought Ends:**
  - Before 2012, India had **never won an Olympic medal in archery** (despite Deepika Kumari being a world #1).
- **The "Curse" of the Host Nation:**
  - Great Britain, Italy, and the USA (all strong archery nations) **failed to medal** in the team event.

---

### **Conclusion**
The **2012 Women’s Team Archery** event was a **thrilling, historic competition**, featuring **South Korea’s dominance, India’s breakthrough, and a dramatic shoot-off for gold**. It remains one of the most **exciting team archery finals** in Olympic history.
